topic.claim: Nearly half of Indian singles deliberately slowing down on dating apps through the festive season isn't them giving up on love, it's them timing it around family, proof that dating apps never actually took family out of the equation, they just moved the negotiation online.
topic.behaviour: A QuackQuack survey of 12,000 Indian daters aged 22-35 found 49% deliberately delaying matches or commitment this festive season to avoid family and social pressure, over 43% of women and 36% of men said they've mistaken festive loneliness for romantic compatibility before, and eight in ten daters aged 23-30 said festival rituals make them more likely to think fondly of an ex.
topic.mechanism: Festive season comes loaded with weddings, family events and expectations piling up all at once, so even people meeting strangers on an app end up making dating decisions around managing that pressure rather than just the relationship itself.
topic.group: Urban daters aged 22-35 on dating apps during festive season
topic.why_now: Published mid festive-wedding season, directly relevant right now

score.why: Real festive-season survey data reframed as dating apps never removing family from the equation, just moving it online, warmer register for range.

edits: slide 1: The opener says 'Almost half' and then '49%', so the number lands twice. Keep 'Almost half of Indian singles are going slow on dating apps this festive season' and drop '49% said' in favour of 'They said they're delaying matches or commitment because of festive pressure.'

slide 1: The last line says apps 'moved the family meeting to your phone', but the data shows people slowing down on the app to avoid family. Swap for something closer to the data, like 'The apps never took family out of dating. Family just decides when you swipe.'

slide 1: Replace 'Nobody wants to take a three-week match to Diwali and face every chacha at once' with a shorter line, such as 'Nobody wants to bring a three-week match to Diwali and face every chacha at once.' This is easier on the first read and keeps the sentence under 15 words.

paragraphs: Almost half of Indian singles are going slow on dating apps this festive season. QuackQuack asked 12,000 daters aged 22-35. They said they're delaying matches or commitment because of festive pressure.
Nobody wants to bring a three-week match to Diwali and face every chacha at once.
The apps never took family out of dating. Family just decides when you swipe.

replaced_after_panel_review.caption: What's the one festive question from a relative that made you pause a chat on a dating app?
replaced_after_panel_review.alt_text: Text post: A QuackQuack survey of 12,000 Indian daters aged 22 to 35 found 49% are delaying matches or commitment this festive season because of festive pressure. The post says this is fair, since nobody wants to face every relative with a new match at Diwali. It ends by saying dating apps never took family out of dating; family just decides when you swipe.

claims.text: 49% are deliberately delaying matches or commitment this festive season because of festive pressure

paragraphs:
Wedding season budget, for one guest:
- Two outfits you'll never wear again
- A shagun envelope you round up so it doesn't look small
- Flights home, booked late
- One sangeet dance you agreed to in a weak moment
The couple will remember none of it. Your credit card will remember all of it.

draft.caption: Which one hit your account hardest this year?
